BiblicalUsage: Chaneph is the impious, the soiled, the hypocrite, and it is always a condition of the heart before it is an act. Isaiah says every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer, and God sends Assyria against a hypocritical nation. Job says the hypocrite's hope shall perish, and that a hypocrite shall not come before God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hypocrite's danger is not that he sins but that he hides it under religion. Job knew the difference: the hypocrite hopes in his own standing, and that hope perishes. I hold that God sees the soil on the heart no washing can hide, and the only cure is the honesty Job finally learned.
